en: The Sūtra on Manifesting the Merits of Boundless Buddha-lands, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was in the tranquil Dharma-park of the kingdom of Magadha.

Vairocana sat upon a lion throne atop a red lotus pedestal, which was adorned with the most exquisite jewels and was as firm as the diamond of the sublime Bodhi; he was accompanied by great bodhisattvas numbering as many as the atoms within ten unspeakably many *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields, and was surrounded before and behind by a vast assembly of gods, humans, asuras, and others.

At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Acintyaprabhāsarāja. Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
“Are there differences in superiority or inferiority regarding the temporal adornments of the various Buddha-lands?
The Buddha said, “Good son!
One eon in this Sahā world, the buddha-field of Śākyamuni Buddha, constitutes a single day and night in the Sukhāvatī world, the buddha-field of Amitābha Buddha;
one eon in the Sukhāvatī world constitutes a single day and night in the Kāṣāyadhvaja world, the buddha-field of Vajradṛḍhapramuditabuddhi Buddha;
and one eon in the Kāṣāyadhvaja world constitutes a single day and night in the Anivartacakranirghoṣa world, the buddha-field of Paramasundaraparipūrṇaraktotpalaśarīra Buddha.
One eon in the world-system of Non-retrogression Wheel Sound is a single day and night in the Dharma Banner Buddha-land of the World Free from Dust;
one eon in the World Free from Dust is a single day and night in the Lion Buddha-land of the World of Bright Lamps;
one eon in the World of Bright Lamps is a single day and night in the Universal Illumination Buddha-land of the World of Wondrous Light.
One eon in the world-system Wondrous Light is a single day and night in the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Dharma-Radiance Emitting from the Body in the world-system Difficult to Transcend;
one eon in the world-system Difficult to Transcend is a single day and night in the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata King of All Supernatural Powers and Wisdom Light in the world-system Adorned;
one eon in the world-system Adorned is a single day and night in the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Moon Awakening in the world-system Mirror Wheel.

“Good son! In this manner, these worlds increase successively until they reach a number equal to the atoms within ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* buddha-fields. One eon in the final buddha-field among those worlds constitutes a single day and night in the Buddha-field of the World Honored One Virtuous Merit (*Bhadraguṇa*) in the Lotus Virtue (*Padmaguṇa*) world. In that world, the assembly of bodhisattvas cultivates the sublime stages of Samantabhadra’s conduct.”

“Good son! Just as the days and nights gradually increase in various worlds, so too do the lifespans, physical forms, and the adornments of the worlds of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; this is because the merit of those sentient beings continues to increase.”

“If there are sons or daughters of good family who, upon hearing this ‘Dharma Gate Revealing the Merits of Boundless Buddha-lands,’ rejoice with faith and reverence, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate it according to the principle, and extensively explain it to others—then at the time of their death, immeasurable Buddhas from the Buddha-lands of the ten directions will all appear before them, comforting, exhorting, and praising them, causing them to increase their immeasurable roots of goodness. They shall be reborn in the pure lands of the Buddhas according to their vows, and until they attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, they shall constantly remember their past lives in every birth, cultivating the bodhisattva practices until they are swiftly brought to fulfillment.”

When the Bhagavat had spoken this sutra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acintyaprabhāsarāja, together with the entire assembly of devas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it.
The Sūtra on Manifesting the Merits of Boundless Buddha-fields.
